A · Finished assembly

Fig. A-1 The finished desk seen from the room. Dashed lines under the front edges: the two steel rails, hidden by the tops. Left and right are as you sit at the inside corner facing the diagonal: top A is on your right, top B on your left.
No.PartNo.Part
P01Top A, EKBACKEN 2490 x 650 x 28P07Rail B, steel angle 2130
P02Top B, EKBACKEN 2490 x 650 x 28P09Round adjustable foot 4 in x 8
P03ALEX 1, drawer unit 360 x 580 x 700P12VIVO STAND-V300CU
P04ALEX 2, storage unit with door 360 x 580 x 700P13Samsung Odyssey G5 32 in

What this desk is

Two IKEA kitchen tops make an L. Top A lies along the back wall and keeps the corner square; top B lies along the side wall and its end butts against top A's front edge. Each top stands 30 mm off its wall, with its square, unfinished long edge toward the wall. The far end of each top rests on an ALEX cabinet through four adjustable feet: the feet are screwed to the top, and their pads drop into printed rings on the cabinet, so the desk cannot slide on the cabinets and the two heavy boxes hold the whole frame square. Six OLOV legs stand along the two wall edges, none at the front, so the space under the inside corner is open for your knees.

That leaves the two front edges with nothing under them for more than two metres, so each one is carried by a steel angle rail screwed to the underside 120 mm back from the front edge. Under the inside corner the two rails are bolted together with two gusseted steel fittings, so the corner of top B hangs from rail A. The rails never touch a cabinet: their ends load the top, and the top loads the nearest feet. The monitor stand clamps to top A's two wall edges, 400 mm from the corner; the surface is 830 mm above the floor.

B · Before you begin

Read this chapter once before you pick up a drill. Budget a weekend: the steel on day one, the assembly on day two.

Safety

Fig. B-1 · The five rules that protect the tops and you.
!
NEVER A FASTENER DEEPER THAN 21 MM INTO A TOP
The EKBACKEN tops are 28 mm particleboard with a thin laminate skin. A screw or pilot that reaches the skin lifts it into a bump you will see and feel for ever. Every screw in this manual stops at least 7 mm short of the top face (28 − 21). If your tops measure 27 mm instead of 28, shorten every screw into the top by 1 mm. If you ever substitute a screw, keep this rule. Chapter D shows every depth.
  • Laminate protection. Spread a blanket on the floor first. The tops lie face down on it, laminate on the blanket, for every marking and drilling step. Never slide or drag steel (rails, fittings, the clamp plates) across the laminate: lift it on and off.
  • Eye protection for every hole drilled in steel; drill at low speed with cutting oil. Gloves while you deburr and file the steel: drilled edges are sharp.
  • Two people to turn a top over and stand it on its legs (2490 long). A helper is also needed to slide the finished desk off and back to the walls.

Work area

Fig. B-2 · Floor needed: 2520 × 3170, including the 30 mm gaps to both walls.

The finished desk needs 2520 × 3170 mm of clear floor in the corner: each top is 2490 long and stands 30 mm off its wall. MEASURE ON HARDWARE Measure both walls (wall to wall) and the baseboard thickness before you start.

You also need floor space for one top at a time lying face down on the blanket (2490 × 650 plus room to kneel all round), and a bench with two clamps for drilling the two 2130 mm steel rails. All steel is drilled on the bench, never under the desk.

Clear the corner before chapter G: the ALEX units are placed by the walls before the tops go on.

Printed tools (P18): print these before you mark anything

All of them are in parts/tools/; parts/README.md has print settings. Print as saved, no supports. Never scale a printed tool in the slicer: its distances are the tool. The lipped and fenced tools print lip-up and are turned over to use.

!
EVERY JIG HOLE IS BIT-SIZED
Hold the jig on, start each pilot 3–4 mm through the jig's hole, lift the jig, then finish the hole to depth with the drill guide's puck. The small centre holes are for a scriber only; nothing is drilled through them.
ToolWhat it doesQty
Edge T-square. Lip over any edge; punch holes at 50 (ring centres on the ALEX), 85 (feet, with the plate's four 1/8 in holes 46.8 apart round it), 100 (legs L2–L6) and 150 (leg L1).1
Leg jig. Lip over the wall edge; an OLOV's centre and its five 1/8 in holes in one placement: 100 pattern for L2–L6 (solid circle), 150 pattern for L1 (dashed circle, ringed holes).1
Feet corner jig. Fences on a far corner of a face-down top; a foot's centre 85/85 from both edges and its four 1/8 in holes 46.8 apart: F2, F4, F7, F8.1
ALEX corner template. Fences on an ALEX corner; ring centre 50/50, the ring's three 5/64 in holes (radius 33) and the three optional ALEX-foot holes (radius 14.5). Top and bottom corners.1
Rail marking gauge. Lip over the angle's edge; pencil notches at 19 (screw line on the flat leg) and 29 (bolt line on the vertical leg).1
Rail drill jig. Lip over the flat leg's free edge; a 1/8 in bore on the 19 line; sight grooves on the station line. PETG.1
Slot plug (fitting-centring-plug). Drops into a fitting's 21 × 12 slot; a 1/8 in bore dead centre, so the pilot cannot wander in the slot's play.2
Pilot drill guide. SET tower (45 for the 1/8 in bit, 35 for the 5/64 in) and five depth pucks: 12 PLATE, 15 LEG, 10 EDGE, 12 ALEX, 25 RAIL. Re-set the bit every time you change it.1 set
Foot height gauge. A C with 102 inside: all eight feet wound to the same height without a ruler.1
Wall gauge. An L: 65 (ALEX back to wall) and 30 (a top's raw edge to wall).1

Also print the eight locating rings (P10) now: parts/structure/foot-ring, PETG or ABS, flange down. Their 51 mm bore depends on the pad diameter you measure (last page of this chapter).

How sure is each number?

Every dimension in this manual carries one of three confidence labels, or a fourth label that is an instruction to you:

VERIFIEDMeasured on the purchased part, or taken from the part's own geometry file (the printed parts).
SOURCE-DEFINEDDefined by the project documents (the build manual): a design position, not a measurement. It is right by definition; you put the part there.
ASSUMPTION / FIELD CHECKAn engineering estimate or a check done on site. Confirm it before you rely on it.
MEASURE ON HARDWARENot yet measured on your parts. Measure it yourself before the step that uses it, and stop if it differs.

D · Component preparation

This chapter marks both tops face down and labels the two rails. Nothing is fixed yet. Every position is in mm from one datum: top A's back-left corner. x runs along the back wall, y along the side wall. Top A covers x 0–2490, y 0–650; top B covers x 0–650, y 650–3140.

Fig. D-1 · The datum and the two tops, seen from above as installed. SOURCE-DEFINED

Which edge is which

Each top has one rounded, laminated long edge: the front. The other long edge is square and unfinished: it goes against the wall. Either short end can become the side-wall end.

Which top is A

The two tops (P01, P02) are identical. A is the one you lay along the back wall; its unfinished edge is y = 0. B lies along the side wall; its unfinished edge is x = 0 and one short end, the joint end (y = 650), butts against A's front edge. Top B is top A turned 90°, never mirrored.

Fig. D-2 · Face-down convention used on every marking drawing. Stand opposite the taped reference edge (top A: at its front edge; top B: at its far end, joint end away from you): the underside is the plan mirrored left to right, so x grows to the LEFT and the datum side (x = 0) is on your RIGHT. Top B uses the same mapping.

Never through the laminate

!
NEVER THROUGH THE LAMINATE
No screw tip and no pilot goes deeper than 21 mm into a 28 mm top: 28 − 21 = 7 mm of wood must remain under the laminate face. Set every pilot depth with the drill guide's puck, never by eye. If a top measures 27 mm, shorten every screw into it by 1 mm.
Fig. D-12 · Every fastener into the tops at its depth, 2:1.
Fig. D-13 · Ring screws go into the ALEX top, not the desk. MEASURE ON HARDWARE panel thickness.

Setting a puck

11
Loosen the chuck. Drop the bit tip-first into the SET tower's hole for that bit (45 for 1/8 in, 35 for 5/64 in), rest the chuck nose on the tower, tighten. Re-set every time you change bits.
12
Stand the puck flat on the surface (on the rail's flat leg for 25 RAIL), bit down its bore, drill until the chuck nose lands on the puck. The hole is then the depth written on the puck.

If your chuck nose is domed, drill one test hole in scrap and measure it first.

E · Steel rail fabrication and drilling

All steel work happens on the bench, before either rail goes near a top. Under the desk you only drive screws and bolts; you never drill steel there. Two identical lengths of 2 × 2 × 3/16 in hot-rolled angle arrive; either can be rail A. All dimensions in mm.

!
MEASURE BEFORE MARKING OR DRILLING MEASURE ON HARDWARE
1 · Tape each rail from end to end and write the length on the tape label. Design length 2130; bought as 84 in = 2133.6. If a rail is under 2130, stop and check before drilling.
2 · Calipers on each angle: legs 50.8, thickness 4.76 (the docs expect about 4.8).
3 · Every station is measured from the labelled end: rail A's wall end, rail B's corner end. The far end carries any extra length. Never centre the hole pattern on the bar and never shift a hole to share out the extra.
1
Label the datum ends. Wrap tape round one end of each rail and write on it: RAIL A · WALL END on one, RAIL B · CORNER END on the other. Measure both rails from those ends (Fig. E-1). File both cut ends of each rail smooth.
Fig. E-1 · The labelled end is 0 for every station. The last hole is at 2105 on both rails, so a longer rail only lengthens the far end beyond it. SOURCE-DEFINED design length; MEASURE ON HARDWARE delivered length.

Mark the stations. Hook the tape over the labelled end and tick every station on the flat leg from that one hook: rail A 35, 280, 540, 800, 1060, 1320, 1580, 1840, 2105; rail B 25, 75, 280, 540, 800, 1060, 1320, 1580, 1840, 2105. Fig. E-5 · One hook, every station. The station line only has to cross the leg; the jig finds the 19.

Pencil the two lines with the rail marking gauge, full length. Screw line: lip over the flat leg's free edge, pencil in the 19 notch, slide. Bolt line: gauge on the vertical leg's outer face, lip over the heel, pencil in the 29 notch, slide. The bolt line is only a check: the fitting's holes must sit on it in step 6.

5
Open and deburr. Jig off. Open every pilot to ⌀5.56 (7/32 in) at low speed with a drop of oil on each; the bit follows the pilot. Deburr both faces with the file or a larger bit turned by hand.
Fig. E-7 · Flat leg in section. The jig's bore is 1/8 in plus a running clearance; it keeps the bit square and on the 19 line.
!
THE FITTING IS THE TEMPLATE VERIFIED
The fittings were measured on 23 Oct 2026: legs 100.5 × 41, two 21 × 12 slots per leg with centres 29.15 and 78.45 from the heel. That puts the six bolt holes at the positions below. Even so, do not lay them out with the tape: clamp the fitting on its heel mark and drill through it with the printed slot plug (steps 6 and 7), so each hole lands on its slot's centre. Check first that a plug drops into each slot without rattle. The heel of a fitting is the outside of its bend.

Floor test. Lay both rails upside down on the floor, flat legs down, vertical legs up. Butt rail B's corner end against the outer face of rail A's vertical leg so that rail B's outer face is on rail A's 520 mark; rail B's flat leg then covers 469 to 520 on rail A's scale. Bolt both fittings on loosely: the outside one on the far-end side of rail B, the inside one on the wall side. Every bolt must slide in by hand. Check the corner with the combination square. F · Steel corner assembly

The two rails are joined at the inside corner by two gusseted strut fittings, one each side of rail B's end, bolted to the vertical legs. This bolted joint, not the joining plates, carries the inside corner of top B. Both tops are standing (build manual step 7); you work from below.

!
SEQUENCE: THE FITTINGS GO ON LAST SOURCE-DEFINED
Before the first fitting goes on, all of these must be done:
1 · The two surfaces are flush at the joint, leveled with the feet (never packed).
2 · Rail B's end touches the outer face of rail A's vertical leg with no gap, and rail B's outer face is on the 520 mark on rail A.
3 · Joining plates P1 and P2 are screwed across the joint. They align the tops; they do not carry the corner.
4 · Rail B's screws 1 and 2 are driven into top A. The inside fitting sits right under them and would block the driver.

Fig. F-2 · Section at the bolt line, seen from above. Datum: top A's back-left corner; x = 530 is 520 from rail A's wall end (rail A starts at x = 10). Arrows: insertion direction. The cut runs along the fitting slots, so their 21 length shows round each bolt.
1
Outside fitting. Heel into the outside corner, one leg flat on rail A's vertical leg toward the far end, the other on rail B's outer face, gusset up, facing the knee space. Push O1 and O2 through from the fitting side with a washer under each head; washer and nut on rail A's inner face. Finger tight.
2
Inside fitting. Into the pocket: heel in the inside corner, one leg on rail A's vertical leg toward the wall end, the other on the inner face of rail B's vertical leg, gusset pointing at the floor. Gusset-up it would sit 1 mm under the head of rail B's screw 1. I1 and I2 from the fitting side, washers, nuts on rail A's inner face. Finger tight.
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 32
L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualF · Steel corner
3
Through bolts. C1 and C2 from the outside fitting: through the outside fitting, rail B's vertical leg and the inside fitting, washer under the head, washer and nut in the pocket. Finger tight. All six bolts are now in; none is tight.
Fig. F-3 · Bolt stack-ups, cut along the bolt. Plates drawn cut off. The fitting's slots are 21 × 12; the cut shows their 12 width. VERIFIED fitting; SOURCE-DEFINED bolts.
4
Check again, then tighten all six. Fingertip across the joint: no step. Rail B's end still touching rail A. Then tighten every bolt fully:
!
TIGHTENING: 25 N·m (18 ft·lb) SOURCE-DEFINED
With a torque wrench, 25 N·m (18 ft·lb), under the standard dry torque even for a grade 2 bolt. Without one, pull as hard as one hand can on a 15 cm wrench, then stop.
Why tight, not snug: this is a friction joint. The fittings' 21 × 12 slots leave 2.5 mm of play across and 11.5 mm along each bolt, the 7/16 in rail holes 1.6 mm, so only the clamping force keeps rail B's corner from settling.
When: only after the two surfaces are flush and rail B's end touches rail A.
Later: if the corner ever drops a millimetre, retighten these six bolts.

H · Joining and positioning the countertops

Two people. Both tops are face down with legs, feet and rails fitted, every OLOV pre-set to 802 (80.2 cm), every pad set with the foot height gauge (102); the ALEX units stand in place with their rings on.

PartsHardwareTools
P01 top A · P02 top B · P03 ALEX 1 · P04 ALEX 2 · P05 OLOV leg · P06 rail A · P07 rail B · P08 strut fitting × 2 · P09 foot · P10 ring · P11 mending plate × 2 (joining) H03 #10 × 1 in × 2 (rail B holes 1, 2) · H04 #10 × 5/8 in × 8 · H05 #10 washer × 8 · H08 3/8-16 × 1-1/2 in bolt × 6 · H09 3/8 washer × 12 · H10 3/8-16 nylon nut × 6 Drill guide (SET tower, pucks 25 RAIL and 12 PLATE), 1/8 in bit, Robertson #2 on a 3 in extension, level, straightedge, tape, torque wrench or 15 cm wrench
1
Stand top A. With a helper, turn top A over and stand it on its legs: lower the ALEX end first so the four pads drop into their rings on ALEX 1, then the leg end. Level along x and along y by turning the OLOV feet and the round feet until it reads flat and all four pads bear with no rock. Target: surface 830 (83.0 cm) at every corner. SOURCE-DEFINED
Fig. H-1 · Top A from the front (1:26). a: ALEX end first, the pads drop into the rings; b: leg end down, level, 830 at both ends. Rail A hangs under the top; it never touches ALEX 1.
Fig. H-2 · Pad into ring (section, 1:2.4). Bore 51 VERIFIED; pad 50 MEASURE ON HARDWARE
!
Once the pads are in the rings, top A cannot be pushed.
If the pads miss, or the top is not 30 (3 cm) off a wall, lift the ALEX end a few millimetres and slide the ALEX unit, not the top. The wall gauge's 30 leg, or a 3 cm offcut, against the wall is the easiest gauge.

830 assumes ALEX units 700 tall ASSUMPTION / FIELD CHECK until measured. With the optional ALEX feet the surface rises by their height (20, 40 or 60).

L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualPage 44

2
Stand top B and slide it home.
  1. Wind top B's OLOV legs 2–3 mm short, so rail B's corner end (it projects 120 past B's end) can slide under top A.
  2. Turn top B over onto its legs with its pads in the rings on ALEX 2.
  3. Push top B (ALEX 2 slides with it) until rail B's corner end touches the outer face of rail A's vertical leg and B's end meets A's front edge at y 650 (65 cm), 30 off the side wall.
  4. Wind B's legs up until the two surfaces are flush.
Fig. H-3 · Top B seen from the knee space, looking at the side wall (1:24); top A cut beyond B's inside edge, ALEX 1 not shown. a: legs short, push; b: home, wind the legs up. The rails rest only on the tops; neither touches an ALEX.
Fig. H-4 · The joint in section, same view (1:2.2). Dashed: top B on its way in, 2–3 mm low. Solid: home. Rail B's flat leg bears on top A's underside for its first 120; its holes 1 and 2 are drilled in step 5.
!
Never force the corner.
If the corner will not meet, or the surfaces will not come flush, adjust leg height, not the joint. Do not hammer, clamp or lever the tops together.

3
Check under the corner, then level the joint. Rail B's end must touch the face of rail A's vertical leg with no gap, and rail B's outer face must line up with the 52.0 cm (520) mark on rail A. If not, lift top B a little and move it. Then bring the two surfaces level at the joint by turning the OLOV feet and the round feet, never by packing anything under the joining plates. A fingertip across the joint finds no step.
4
Joining plates P1 and P2, from below. Screw each plate on the outline you drew: y 533–787 (53.3–78.7 cm), long axis along y, centred x 150 and 350. They are not centred on the joint: each starts 3 clear of rail A. Pilot every hole 1/8 in, 12 deep, with the drill guide's 12 PLATE puck held up overhead; drive H04 #10 × 5/8 in with an H05 washer. Two screws in each top. SOURCE-DEFINED
Fig. H-5 · The corner from above, looking through the tops (1:5). Datum: top A's back-left corner, x along the back wall, y along the side wall. Plate holes at 20, 70, 184 and 234 from the plate end nearest rail A. Dashed: OLOV plates L1 and L4, and the two fittings (orientation in chapter F).

5
Rail B meets top A. Through rail B's holes 1 and 2 (25 and 75 from its corner end, both under top A) drill a 1/8 in pilot with the drill guide's 25 RAIL puck on the flat leg: 4.8 of steel plus 20 into the wood. 6
Bolt on the two fittings, then tighten. Orientation is in chapter F: outside fitting heel at the outside corner, inside fitting heel at the inside corner with its gusset pointing at the floor.
  1. Rail A: four H08 bolts from the fitting side, H09 washer under each head, washer and H10 nylon-insert nut on the inside of the leg. Finger-tight.
  2. Rail B: two H08 bolts through outside fitting, leg and inside fitting, washer each end, H10 nut. Finger-tight.
  3. Only when the surfaces are flush (step 3) and rail B's end touches rail A: tighten all six to 25 N·m (18 ft·lb); without a torque wrench, one hand's full pull on a 15 cm wrench, then stop. SOURCE-DEFINED

Tight, not snug: the fittings' 21 × 12 slots leave 2.5 of play across and 11.5 along each bolt, and the 7/16 in rail holes 1.6, so only the clamping force holds the corner. Fitting legs 100.5 × 41, 5 thick; slot centres 29.15 and 78.45 from the heel VERIFIED. Rail bolt holes: rail A 549.2 and 598.5 (outside fitting) and 485.9 and 436.6 (inside fitting) from the wall end; rail B 29.2 and 78.5 from the corner end VERIFIED.

7
Checks. Do every one; if one fails, fix it with the feet or the legs, never at the joint.
Fig. H-6 · The checks in plan (1:28). Datum: top A's back-left corner.
  • Square: the butt joint is closed across its full 650 width (no light), rail B's end touches rail A, rail B's outer face is on rail A's 520 mark.
  • Level: a level across the joint and along it reads flat both ways; a fingertip finds no step.
  • Height: surface 830 ± 3 at all six outer corners, 1–6. SOURCE-DEFINED
  • Pads: all eight bear. Turn each of F1–F8 by hand in its ring: none spins free or rocks.
!
FIELD CHECK, not in the build manual ASSUMPTION / FIELD CHECK
Optional 3-4-5 triangle at the inside corner: mark 600 along A's front edge and 800 along B's inside edge; the diagonal between the marks is 1000 when the L is square. Write down what it reads. If it is off, check the butt joint for a gap first, then move ALEX 2 with top B on it. Never force the corner.

The corner load test (20 kg on top B's inside corner), the sideways push and the settling record are in the final checks. Never stand or sit on the corner.

!
Do this after chapter I.

Parts P19 (corner, two 80 fillers, two clamp pieces, 240 segments, connector tiles), H07 #4 × 1/2 in flat head, the drill guide's 10 EDGE puck with a 5/64 in bit, the wall gauge.

8
Measure, set, print. With the desk in place against both walls, measure the gap between each top's raw back edge and the wall at five or six points along each wall. Set gap in parts/accessories/wall-gap-common.scad to the smallest value minus 1 and print the trim. MEASURE ON HARDWARE (design gap 30, so gap 29 as saved).

Build each chain from the corner outward. Corner piece, 80 filler, clamp piece with its notch round the clamp back, then the 240 segments (slotted ones where the cut list says), ending with the short piece. Butt every joint and push a connector tile up into the pockets.
Fig. H-8 · Chain order along both walls, desk positions in mm from the corner (1:20). The notch (white, in K) wraps the clamp back, 80 long and 17.5 proud VERIFIED.
Fig. H-9 · Connector tile (1.8:1), one under every joint, pins up. It bridges the 20 × 12 pockets of two butted pieces.

Every piece, the corner included, has a pocket on its underside at each end, over the gap. Butt two pieces, then push a tile up into both pockets until its pins seat: the joint cannot step, bow or drift, and nothing shows on top.

If a wall is out and the notch misses the clamp, change the 80 filler's seg and reprint it, nothing else.

The VIVO STAND-V300CU (P12) has two independent C-clamps and no base bar. Both clamp onto top A's own wall edges, never on the joint: clamp 1 centred at x = 400 (40.0 cm) on the back edge, clamp 2 centred at y = 400 (40.0 cm) on the side-wall end. The crossbar runs on the diagonal between the poles. Each lower jaw bears on a spare steel mending plate (P11), because particleboard crushes under a bare steel jaw over months. 1

Lay the pad plates. Lay a spare mending plate P11 flat on the underside, on each pad outline drawn when top A was marked, long side along the edge: x 200–454, y 5–81 at clamp 1; y 200–454, x 5–81 at clamp 2. Loose, no screws: the jaw holds it. SOURCE-DEFINED

J · Final inspection and load testing

Ten checks, in the build manual's order, before you call the desk done. Each is an ACCEPTANCE CHECK: a pass or fail you can see or measure. Several of them test a STRUCTURAL ESTIMATE from the design review that has not been measured on this desk; the check says which. Write the results in the boxes and in the sign-off table at the end of this chapter. Datum for every drawing: top A's back-left corner (0, 0); mm.

Check 1 · Surface height at the six corners ACCEPTANCE CHECK

1

Measure from the floor to the top face at each of the six corners of the L (Fig. J-1). Every reading 830 ± 3 (83.0 cm). With the optional ALEX feet fitted: 830 plus their height. If a corner is out, turn that corner's OLOV foot or round foot, then measure all six again.

Fig. J-1a The six corners, numbered for the record.
Fig. J-1b Tape from the floor to the top face, at the corner.
Corner123456
Reading (mm)

2

Fig. J-2 Plan of the joint at y = 650. 1, 2: level positions; 3: fingertip; 4: where the straightedge of check 5 goes, at the inside corner.

Check 3 · Corner load test ACCEPTANCE CHECK

!
NEVER STAND OR SIT ON THE DESK
The test load is a known weight: 20 kg of water and books. Do not stand or sit on the corner; that is not what the beam was sized for.
Fig. J-3a Plan. Case faces 100 in from top B's front edge and from the joint (case size schematic). R: reading point.
3

Set 20 kg (a case of water plus a few books) on top B's inside corner, 100 (10 cm) in from both edges.

Rest a straightedge from leg L1's line across the corner. Read the drop at the corner (R): no more than 2. The estimate is about 1. STRUCTURAL ESTIMATE

Lift the weight off. The corner returns to where it was, nothing creaks, no screw or bolt has moved.

Tests: sag at the inside corner (rail A carrying rail B's corner reaction) and corner-joint slip (the six fitting bolts holding by friction). STRUCTURAL ESTIMATE

Drop under 20 kgReturned?Creak / movement?

4

Tests: the racking estimate (eight pads captive in their rings hold the frame against a sideways push) and the ALEX load share. STRUCTURAL ESTIMATE

Fig. J-4 Foot P09 on its pad in ring P10 on the ALEX top.

5

6

K · Maintenance and troubleshooting

Schedule

WhenDoSee
Day 0Write down the step at the joint (straightedge at the inside corner).Check 5, Fig. J-5
Two weeksRetighten every screw. Straightedge at the joint again; if the corner has settled, retighten the six fitting bolts to 25 N·m. Look at each printed ring and its three screws.Checks 5 and 10; troubleshooting
One monthStraightedge at the joint again; retighten the six fitting bolts if it settled.Check 5
Any timeIf the corner ever drops a millimetre, retighten the six fitting bolts.Corner bolts, below
!
NEVER DEEPER THAN 21 MM INTO A TOP
The tops are 28 mm particleboard with a thin laminate skin; a screw reaching the skin lifts it. Replace a screw only with the same size. If a top measured 27, every screw into it is 1 mm shorter. SOURCE-DEFINED

Corner bolts

Boltssix 3/8-16 × 1-1/2 in hex bolts, grade 5 (H08), washer under head and nut (H09), nylon-insert nuts (H10): four through rail A's vertical leg, two through rail B's leg with a fitting on each side Torque25 N·m (18 ft·lb); without a torque wrench, pull as hard as one hand can on a 15 cm wrench, then stop Whya friction joint: each fitting leg has two 21 × 12 mm slots, centred 29.15 and 78.45 from the heel VERIFIED; they leave each bolt 2.5 of play across and 11.5 along, and the rails' 7/16 in holes 1.6, so only the clamping force keeps rail B's corner from settling Ordertighten only with the two surfaces flush and rail B's end touching rail A

The mending plates across the joint align the tops; they do not carry the corner. SOURCE-DEFINED

L-Shaped Corner Desk · Assembly ManualK · Troubleshooting

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Corner has dropped; step at the joint grewThe six fitting bolts lost clamping force (friction joint); supports settlingBring the surfaces flush with the OLOV feet and the round feet, never by packing anything under the joining plates. Check rail B's end still touches rail A. Retighten all six bolts to 25 N·m. Write the new step down (Fig. J-5).
Top moves on its ALEX, or a pad spins or rocksA pad is out of its ring or not bearingLift that ALEX end a few millimetres and slide the ALEX unit, not the top, until the pads drop into their rings. Each foot set with the 102 gauge, no rock. Level along x and y; re-check 830 at the corners (Figs. J-1, J-4).
Printed ring cracked or its screws looseRing wall overloaded by a sideways pushInspect at two weeks. A crack: reprint the ring (parts/structure/foot-ring.stl), PETG or ABS, flange-down: 51 bore, 3 wall, 75 × 2.5 flange. Refit with #6 × 5/8 in flat-head screws (H06), 5/64 in pilots 12 mm deep (12 ALEX puck). Never run the desk with a ring missing.
Leg moves or wobblesOLOV plate screws looseRetighten the five M4 × 16 mm screws (H01). A screw that spins: repair the hole (below), re-pilot 1/8 in, 15 mm deep (15 LEG puck). Re-set the OLOV to 802 (80.2 cm), or the ALEX-feet table's number.
Monitor clamp creepsClamp loosened over timeRetighten the clamp with the crossbar fitted. Keep the steel plate (P11) flat on its outline under the jaw. Never add a soft pad under the jaw.
Screw spins (stripped)Hole worn in the particleboardBack it out, fill the hole with wood glue and a couple of matchsticks, let it dry, re-pilot.
A mark is off by more than 2 mmMarking errorRedraw it. A stray 1/8 in hole in the underside does no harm.
A fitting bolt will not go inHoles not quite in lineOpen the hole in the rail with a round file; never force it.
Fig. K-1 A screw that spins: back it out, fill the hole with wood glue and a couple of matchsticks, let it dry, re-pilot with the step's own bit and depth.

Every fix above is from the build manual and the build guide SOURCE-DEFINED.
